judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: I drove the live page in headless Edge at 1280x800 and tabbed to this owl-carousel arrow in the 'Hcor explica' section. The site removes the outline (computed outline: none) and the only focus cue is the rule '.carousel .owl-prev/.owl-next:focus {transform: scale(1.08)}': the pale #e9f2ec button grows by about 1.5 px a side on a white section, about 1.13:1, and its green chevron is about 2.5:1 against the button. Nothing that marks the focused state reaches 3:1, so the indicator fails 1.4.11 (F78 lists 1.4.11 for styling that leaves the focus indicator effectively invisible). The owl 'disabled' class on the prev button is not exposed or styled as inactive, and the button stays in the tab order, so the inactive exception does not apply. Rampa's 'next to #e9f2ec' is a loose way to name the neighbouring colour, but the conclusion holds.

On the live page its focus outline is removed (outline: none), and the only change on focus is '.button-default:focus {opacity: .95}', which moves the button from #6ac0d5 to about #66bad0 on the dark footer. judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: This is the 'Agendamentos' top-level menu item (li) in the desktop mega-menu. On the live page at 1280x800, hovering it shows the CSS-hover submenu (.menu-bar-item:hover > .menu-bar-subitems), which covers the hero banner and the quick-access boxes. Pressing Esc without moving the pointer leaves it shown, because the only keyup handler acts on .js-sidenav-active. No other mechanism dismisses it. The 1.4.13 Understanding names sub-menus as covered content, and the obscuring exemption does not apply, so the dismissible requirement fails as reported.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The claim is that pressing 'I' with focus on the body changes the page. I listed the live page's key listeners over CDP: there are only Bootstrap's delegated dropdown keydown/keyup handlers and a jQuery body keyup that reacts to Esc (keyCode 27). Nothing handles 'I'. In repeated trials, screen changes came at random with 'I', 'i', Shift+I and other letters alike. They match the hero carousel's autoplay (the region 13,151 to 1267,714) and the animated WhatsApp popup, not the key press. The probe credited an autoplay change to the key. There is no single-character shortcut, so 2.1.4 does not fail.
